question: Which of the following protected area of Odisha has been declared the 107th National Park of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Satkosia National Park**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Satkosia National Park** was declared as the **107th National Park of India**, located in Odisha. It is known for its unique biodiversity and natural beauty.
 
• The park is situated across the districts of **Angul, Nayagarh, Boudh, and Cuttack** and covers an area of approximately **963.87 square kilometers**.
 
• Satkosia is renowned for its **Satkosia Gorge**, formed by the Mahanadi River as it cuts through the Eastern Ghats, creating a stunning landscape.
 
• The park is home to numerous species, including the endangered **Gharial crocodile**, as well as diverse flora and fauna, making it a significant conservation site.
 
• Satkosia National Park serves as a critical habitat for species such as **tigers, leopards, elephants, and various bird species**. It is also a popular ecotourism destination.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Simlipal National Park:**

 
 
• Located in Mayurbhanj district, Odisha, Simlipal is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**. It covers an area of approximately **2,750 square kilometers**.
 
• The park is known for its **Bengal Tigers**, Asian elephants, and other wildlife species. It also houses beautiful waterfalls like **Barehipani** and **Joranda**.
 
 
 
• **Bhitarkanika National Park:**
 
 
• Located in Kendrapara district, Odisha, Bhitarkanika is famous for its **mangrove forests** and **saltwater crocodiles**.
 
• The park is a Ramsar site and covers an area of approximately **672 square kilometers**.
 
• It is home to diverse wildlife, including migratory birds, monitor lizards, and turtles.
 
 
 
• **Nandankanan National Park:**
 
 
• Located near Bhubaneswar, Odisha, Nandankanan is a **zoological park** rather than a protected national park.
 
• It is famous for its **white tigers** and serves as a major tourist attraction with a wide range of exotic animals.
 
• Nandankanan also has the distinction of being the first zoo to join the **World Association of Zoos and Aquariums (WAZA)**.
 
 
 
• **Protected Areas of India:**
 
 
• India has a total of **107 National Parks** and over **500 Wildlife Sanctuaries**, forming a significant part of its ecological conservation efforts.
 
• National parks are governed by the **Wildlife Protection Act of 1972**, ensuring strict conservation measures.
 
• These areas aim to protect endangered species, biodiversity, and ecosystems unique to the region.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The declaration of Satkosia National Park as the **107th National Park** of India highlights the government’s focus on conserving biodiversity and promoting ecotourism.
 
• While Simlipal and Bhitarkanika are already established national parks, they cater to specific ecological niches such as mangroves and tiger reserves.
 
• Protected areas like Satkosia help in safeguarding endangered species such as the **Gharial crocodile** and preserving the natural beauty of Odisha’s landscapes.
 
• India’s growing network of protected areas underscores its commitment to global conservation goals like the **Aichi Targets** and the **Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD)**.
